PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
To: Christine M. Archer, General Counsel (Pinnacle Industrial Technologies, Inc.)
From: Whitmore & Kessler LLP
Re: Compliance gap analysis - draft DEF 14A (2025 Annual Meeting, June 12, 2025; target filing April 28, 2025)

BOTTOM LINE
The draft should not be filed in its current form. Seven items are filing-critical: (1) an omitted Item 404(a) related-party transaction (Chen/Broadleaf) that also undermines the independence and Proposal 5 disclosures; (2) an annual incentive payout mismatch between the SCT and the Committee's approved amounts, with a payout calculation that does not reproduce; (3) a deficient Pay Versus Performance section; (4) an inaccurate and incomplete insider trading policy disclosure; (5) an unanalyzed Frederickson/Isaacs Clearway relationship, internal D&O discrepancies, and a wrong overboarding conclusion; (6) Proposal 5 eligibility and process; (7) beneficial ownership and equity plan table errors. The in-house checklist (93% complete) overstates readiness. Law was applied from my knowledge of Regulation S-K/Schedule 14A; online fetch of primary text was blocked, so cite-check before reliance.

TIER 1 - CRITICAL (fix before filing)

1. Undisclosed related-person transaction: Broadleaf Consulting (Item 404(a); Item 407(a); Rule 14a-9)
Chen's D&O questionnaire (Feb. 25, 2025) reports $380,000 paid in FY2024 to Broadleaf, in which her spouse holds about a 20% equity interest and shares in profits. A spouse is an immediate family member, the amount exceeds $120,000, and the interest is indirect but material. The draft discloses only Goss and Harmon Properties; checklist R-04 ("no additional transactions") and the cover email ("only" two) are wrong. Required: Item 404(a) disclosure (name, relationship, interest, dollar amount, approval).
Collateral problems: (a) The draft says the Audit Committee administers the RPT policy, but N&G (Chair: Chen, recused; only Halpern acted) approved Broadleaf on March 14, 2024; reconcile and have the Audit Committee ratify. (b) Item 407(a)(3) requires describing relationships the Board considered; the draft says none exist. Chen's analysis (below the NYSE 303A.02(b)(v) $1M/2% test) suggests no bright-line bar, but the Board must make and minute the determination. (c) Chen is the Lead Independent Director relied on to oppose Proposal 5, inviting a Rule 14a-9 challenge. (d) Confirm Chen's Axton start date (2017 vs 2019).

2. Annual incentive: SCT vs approved payouts, and the payout math (Items 402(b), 402(c), 402(d); Rule 14a-9)
The Committee approved (Feb. 20, 2025) payouts at 140% of target: Villanueva $1,813,000; Langford $875,000; Poole $724,500; Isaacs $705,600; Archer $642,600. The SCT "Non-Equity Incentive Plan" column instead reports target amounts (Villanueva $1,295,000 etc.), so each NEO's SCT total is understated (Villanueva by $518,000: about $6,387,800, not $5,869,800), which flows into the pay ratio (about 94.7:1, not 87:1), Proposal 2, the Summary highlights, and Pay Versus Performance. The email ("confirmed at target for SCT") reflects a misunderstanding; Item 402(c)(2)(vii) requires amounts earned.
The draft CD&A states a 140% payout but (i) shows no metric-level factors (checklist C-06 admits this), (ii) states the "no discretion" formulaic payout, yet the 140% does not reproduce. Using the draft's own scale, linear interpolation gives about 124% (EBITDA), 124% (revenue), 87.5% (FCF), blended about 117%. Using the minutes' scale, EBITDA is about 119%, revenue about 134%, FCF 87.5% (the minutes show 57.5%), blended about 117%. The minutes' factors of 155%, 170% and 57.5% are inconsistent with their own stated interpolation. If 140% is wrong, the Company may have overpaid and the "no discretion" statement is untrue; if the Committee intended discretion, it must be disclosed. Before filing: Committee and Rothwell must recompute and document the plan terms; correct SCT, Grants table, CD&A and pay ratio; consider whether a clawback/recoupment or correction of payments is needed.
Additional draft/minutes mismatches: target bonus percentages (draft 110/105/105/95% vs minutes 100/90/90/85%); performance scales (EBITDA threshold/max, revenue, FCF max); NEO titles (Poole, Isaacs, Archer) affecting Item 402(a)(3); peer group size (16 vs 20) and unnamed peers (Item 402(b)(2)(xiv)); director RSU vesting terms. Also: SCT shows only 2024 and 2023 (Item 402(c) requires three years; checklist C-15 claims 2022); Archer's SCT "change in pension/NQDC" column of $67,300 is described as 401(k) matching "earnings," which is not reportable there (no pension; no above-market NQDC earnings) and likely double counts, so her total is overstated; PSU goals for the 2024-2026 awards are not disclosed; no outstanding PSUs from 2023 grants appear in the Outstanding Equity Awards table although 2023 stock awards were reported; Villanueva has 7 years' pension credited service though she joined about 2017 and the plan froze to new participants Jan. 1, 2015 (verify eligibility; Poole/Isaacs/Langford hire dates likewise); pension valuation assumptions (Item 402(h)) are not stated.

3. Pay Versus Performance (Item 402(v))
(a) Only three years (2022-2024) are shown. For a proxy filed in 2025 the table must cover five years (2020-2024) unless the Company is a smaller reporting company (it is a large accelerated filer); the email and checklist C-23 are wrong. (b) FY2023 PEO is misidentified: Harmon was CEO through Dec. 31, 2023; Villanueva (COO) was not PEO. FY2023 PEO SCT and CAP columns (and the footnote's "PEO-equivalent" rationale) must be restated, and PEO columns must be shown for both individuals where the PEO changed. (c) No component reconciliation of SCT to CAP and no list of non-PEO NEOs per year. (d) Values change after item 2. The measure list (five) and the relationship narrative are present.

4. Insider trading policy and hedging disclosure (Items 407(i), 408(b))
The draft says the policy prohibits hedging by "directors and executive officers." The policy actually covers all directors, officers and employees (and family and controlled entities). Item 407(i) requires describing the categories of persons covered; the draft understates scope. Item 408(b) requires disclosing whether the Company has adopted insider trading policies and procedures governing trading by directors, officers, employees (or the registrant itself), with an explanation if not, and filing the policy as an exhibit (Ex. 19) to the 10-K; the draft contains no 408(b) statement, and checklist E-07 asserts compliance. The policy does not address the Company's own transactions in its securities; either adopt procedures or disclose why not. The policy also says nothing on pledging or margin accounts, yet checklist C-13 and the CD&A refer to "anti-hedging and pledging"; do not claim a pledging prohibition. Version control: policy is dated "amended September 15, 2023" yet names Villanueva as CEO (appointed Jan. 1, 2024), Goss, and the October 2023 clawback policy; confirm the true amendment date before filing it as an exhibit. 

5. Compensation Committee interlocks, director data and overboarding (Items 401(e), 407(a), 407(e)(4))
Frederickson's questionnaire discloses that she and NEO David Isaacs serve together on the Clearway Logistics board while she chairs the Committee that sets his pay. The draft contains no Item 407(e)(4) statement and checklist D-11 marks it "N/A - no interlocks" without analysis. A technical interlock under Item 407(e)(4)(iii) arises only if she is (or during FY2024 was) an executive officer of Clearway; the draft bio says she was Clearway's CHRO until 2017, the questionnaire says she is an independent director. Resolve facts, document the analysis, add the Item 407(e)(4) section, and have the Board consider the relationship in its independence and Committee-independence findings.
Frederickson's draft biography conflicts with her questionnaire on employer (Clearway CHRO/Dalton Capital vs Meridian SVP, no employer), Clearway start (2018 vs 2017), chair start (2020 vs 2019) and MBA; Item 401(e) requires accuracy; get corrected confirmation. She also sits on three other public boards (Clearway, Northgate, TerraVerde since Feb. 2025), so four with Pinnacle; checklist D-15 ("no one on more than three") is wrong. Disclose, and check the Corporate Governance Guidelines/ISS/Glass Lewis limits; consider her Committee workload. Also: checklist D-13 applies a Nasdaq rule to an NYSE company; board meetings are seven (draft) vs eight (checklist); Dr. Mehta's profile omits how he was identified (Item 407(c)(2)(vii)), other directorships, and a nominee consent statement (Rule 14a-4(d)).

6. Proposal 5 - Leland Cross (Rule 14a-8)
The email says Leland Cross bought its 6.8% stake in Q4 2024 and submitted on Jan. 15, 2025, and that eligibility was verified as $25,000 for one year. Those facts are irreconcilable: a holder that acquired in Q4 2024 could not have held continuously for one year by Jan. 15, 2025, so Rule 14a-8(b)(1)(i) was not satisfied unless a shorter-tenure tier applies (it does not for a one-year holder of this size; the $15,000/two-year and $2,000/three-year alternatives also fail). Confirm proof of ownership (broker letter), the date of first acquisition (13D/13G), and whether a deficiency notice was timely sent within 14 days under 14a-8(f). The 80-day no-action window under 14a-8(j) has passed (about Feb. 7, 2025); including the proposal voluntarily is permissible, but the Company should document the decision and avoid representing that it "verified" eligibility. Word limit (500 words, 14a-8(d)) is met by the proponent. The Company's opposition statement is not word-limited but is subject to Rule 14a-9: confirm Rule 14a-8(m)(3) delivery of the opposition statement to the proponent at least 30 days before filing (by about March 29), and revise statements that are inaccurate or one-sided: Harmon's ownership (1,620,000 vs 1,740,000 in the table), the "independence" of the Lead Independent Director (Item 1), and omission of Harmon's lease and son-in-law relationships. Also correct the proposal's shares/percent if Leland Cross's 13D/G differs.

TIER 2 - HIGH

7. Beneficial ownership (Item 403): The draft summary and Board statements say Harmon owns 1,620,000 shares (1.96%); the table shows 1,740,000 (2.11%) including options. Use consistent language ("including 120,000 options"). Percentages should add each holder's options to the denominator (the group's 4.86% divides by 82.6M only; the correct figure is about 4.80%); checklist B-03/B-04 claim RSUs and options were handled correctly, but no RSUs appear. The 5% table is "based on 13D/13G filings" without dates; the email names the 9% holder "Vanguard Capital Management LLC" while the draft names "Saxonbrook Capital Management LLC" (and Okonkwo's former employer is Saxonbrook Automation Systems); verify the holder's identity against filings. Share counts as of March 15 should be reconciled with the April 14 record date. Pledging (Item 403(b)) footnote is absent.
8. Equity compensation plan table (Item 201(d)): column (a) totals 2,100,000 but footnote components total 2,185,000 (1,240,000 + 860,000 + 85,000); PSUs appear missing; the checklist says the 2012 Plan was not shareholder-approved while the table lists none unapproved. Reconcile; describe any non-approved plan's features.
9. Section 16(a) (Item 405): The late Form 4 reports an 18,000-RSU grant to Poole on March 15, 2024, whereas the grant table shows 8,264 RSUs (plus 12,396 target PSUs); reconcile the transaction. Verify no other late filings.
10. Rule 14a-5(e)/14a-19 universal proxy: The 2026 deadlines section omits the Rule 14a-19 notice deadline (60 calendar days before the anniversary of the meeting, about April 13, 2026); checklist G-18 treats Rule 14a-19 as "not applicable," which is incorrect for any annual meeting with director elections. Add it, and confirm the proxy card complies.
11. Notice-and-access: draft says full set mailed; checklist says Notice and Access. Align legend, Rule 14a-16 timing and card.
12. Proposals 1 and 4: ten nominees stand for nine seats if Proposal 4 fails, with a post-vote withdrawal of Dr. Mehta; clarify handling of votes, the basis for a stockholder vote (DGCL 109, 141(b), 216; bylaws not provided) and the vote standard. Annex A redline is blank and must be completed.
13. Goss/Harmon Properties: add dollar value of the related person's interest and aggregate lease payments over the term (about $684,000 for the renewal).

TIER 3 - MODERATE
14. Say-on-pay frequency: state when next frequency vote occurs (Item 24). 15. Virtual meeting: add tech support, question procedures, stockholder list access. 16. Pay ratio: recompute after item 2; do not annualize seasonal/temporary workers. 17. Minor: equity award values off $58.14 price; blank cover boxes and skills matrix; Harmon bio dates conflict.

CHECKLIST CORRECTIONS: reopen R-04, D-11, D-15, D-13, G-18, C-06, C-15, C-23/E-04, E-07, B-06, E-01/E-02, R-01.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: Committee/Board action on payout recompute and Chen independence/RPT ratification; corrected D&O confirmations; revise SCT, CD&A, pay ratio, PvP; add missing Item 404, 407, 408(b), 14a-19 text; Proposal 5 eligibility file; conform checklist. The April 25 solicitor hand-off is at risk.
